# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

- Blind gestured: ✋ ✋ (two hands)

Or maybe ✋ = 5 (a hand has 5 fingers) and ✊ = 1? Then Mute's earlier ✊✌ = 1,2. And ✊✊✊ = 1,1,1 or 3. Now the sequence ✋✊✊✊✋✊✋✊✊✋✊ = 5,1,1,1,5,1,5,1,1,5,1. Sum? 

Alternatively ✋ = 5, ✊ = 1: sequence sums to 5+1+1+1+5+1+5+1+1+5+1 = 27.

Hmm, hard to know. But the LIGHT going dark is the critical thing. The light is the timer. Yellow→blue→dark suggests it's running out (dark = about to detonate, or dark = off).

Wait — maybe the light cycles and dark is a state that means "now." Or the sequence yellow, blue, dark is a countdown and we're nearly out of time.

Actually, maybe the light colour corresponds to which wire to cut, and the manual (Mute has it) says: if light is X, cut wire Y. The light is changing, so we need to act at the right moment or the right colour.

I must relay "light is now dark" urgently and push for the manual reading. Mute keeps gesturing but I can't decode. I need Mute to give me the manual reading in a decodable way.

Problem: Mute can't speak, only gesture. I can't decode gestures. But I CAN speak to Mute, and Mute can hear me. Mute can also hear Blind. So Mute can understand everything I say. The bottleneck is Mute→me.

Idea: I can propose a gesture code and have Mute confirm via gesture. But that's slow. 

Better idea: Blind can hear me AND can speak. Blind can also gesture. So Blind could relay Mute's words? But Blind can't hear Mute (Mute can't speak). Hmm. Mute can only gesture. Blind can see gestures. So Blind sees Mute's gestures. But Blind can't decode them either unless Mute's gestures are meaningful.

Wait — actually, can Blind see Mute's gestures? Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind CANNOT see gestures! So Blind cannot see Mute's gestures. Only I (Deaf) and... who else can see gestures? Mute can see gestures (Mute sees my gestures). Deaf sees gestures. Blind cannot.

So gesture channel: Mute↔Deaf (both see gestures). Blind is out of the gesture channel entirely.

So the only ones who can see gestures are Mute and me. And Mute can't speak, I can't hear. So Mute and I communicate purely by gesture. Blind communicates by speech (heard by Mute and me... no, I can't hear). Blind's speech is heard by Mute only. And Blind's gestures are seen by nobody? Wait, Blind gestured to Deaf and I received it. So I CAN see Blind's gestures. Let me recheck: "Blind gestures to Deaf: ✋ ✋" — I received it. So Blind's gestures reach me. So Blind CAN gesture and I see it.

Hmm, but Blind "cannot see a gesture" — that's about receiving, not making. Blind can make gestures (using hands), and those are seen by whoever can see (Mute and me). So Blind's gestures reach both Mute and me.

OK so gesture channel: everyone can send gestures; receivers are those who can see = Mute and Deaf. Blind can send but not receive gestures.

Speech channel: senders Mute? No, Mute can't speak. Senders: Blind and Deaf. Receivers: those who can hear = Mute and Blind. Deaf can't hear.

So:
- Deaf's speech → Mute, Blind hear it.
- Deaf's gesture → Mute sees it (Blind can't see).
- Blind's speech → Mute hears it (Deaf can't hear).
- Blind's gesture → Mute and Deaf see it.
- Mute's gesture → Deaf sees it (Blind can't see). Mute's speech → none (can't speak).

So Mute's only output is gesture, seen only by Deaf. Mute can only ever talk to me! And I can only reach Mute by gesture, and reach both by speech.

This means: Mute → Deaf is the ONLY path for the manual. Mute must gesture the manual to me, and I must decode it. And I must then SPEAK it to Blind (since Blind can't see gestures).

So the whole plan hinges on Mute and me agreeing on a gesture code. Mute has been gesturing to me (✊✌, ✊✊✊, the long sequence). I need to decode.

Given Mute's gestures use ✊ (fist) and ✋ (hand) and ✌ (peace): maybe Mute is encoding numbers. ✊ = 1 finger? No, a fist has 0 fingers. ✋ = 5 fingers (open hand). ✌ = 2 fingers. 👆 = 1 finger. 

If symbols = finger counts: ✊=0, 👆=1, ✌=2, ✋=5. Hmm.

Mute's sequence: ✋ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✋ ✊ ✋ ✊ ✊ ✋ ✊ = 5,0,0,0,5,0,5,0,0,5,0. Doesn't look like much.

Hmm. This is getting speculative. Let me step back.

The most important thing: the LIGHT is now DARK. This is likely the end of the countdown. I must relay it and push hard for the manual.

I'll speak to both, emphasizing the dark light, and I'll gesture to Mute asking for the manual in a simple yes/no form. Actually, I can ask Mute yes/no questions and Mute answers with 👍/👎. Let me do that. I'll ask Mute a series of yes/no questions about the manual, and Mute answers with 👍/👎. That's the fastest path.

But I should be careful not to waste the turn. Let me ask the most critical questions.

Let me send a clear message to Mute establishing the yes/no code and asking key questions, and speak to Blind to relay the dark light and ask what Blind feels.

Also, I realize I should tell Blind the key structural fact: Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute can only reach me via gesture, and I relay to Blind by speech. Blind should speak their findings to Mute (who hears) and me... no, I can't hear Blind's speech. So Blind's findings reach Mute only. Blind must gesture to reach me. Ugh, but Blind can gesture and I see it. So Blind can reach me by gesture. But Blind can't see my gestures, so I must reply to Blind by speech.

OK. Let me just act.

Calls:
- speak(to="mute"): establish yes/no code, relay dark light, ask manual questions.
- speak(to="blind"): relay dark light, ask what they feel, explain channel structure.
- gesture(to="mute"): 👆 again (light changed) — or maybe a new symbol for "dark". I'll gesture 👇 to mean "light is dark/down"? I'll name it in speech: "I gesture 👇 to mean the light is dark."

Let me write it.I'm the Deaf monkey. **The LIGHT is now [dark]** — it went yellow → blue → dark. That's a progression: the light is cycling/counting down. This is almost certainly a timer running out. Urgent. DISPLAY still [0], WIRES unchanged.

New arrivals:
- Mute gestured a long sequence: ✋ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✋ ✊ ✋ ✊ ✊ ✋ ✊
- Blind gestured: ✋ ✋

Critical structural insight I should now act on: **Mute's only output is gesture, and only I can see it.** Blind cannot see gestures at all. So the manual can only reach the group through Mute→Deaf by gesture, and I must then speak it to Blind. The bottleneck is decoding Mute's gestures.

Fastest fix: establish a yes/no code. Mute hears my speech, so I can *name* the code and Mute can answer. I'll ask Mute to gesture 👍 = yes, 👎 = no, and I'll name a symbol for "light is dark."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. URGENT: the light is now DARK. It went yellow, then blue, then dark — it is counting down. Display still 0, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green. I cannot decode your long gesture. Let us use a code: gesture thumbs-up for YES, thumbs-down for NO. I am gesturing a downward finger to mean 'the light is dark.' ```
```
